_doc: Opt-in changes a release brings to existing homelab repos: things init_repo.py --sync-managed must NOT do
by itself (user-owned files, config choices, snapshots to regenerate, steps on external systems).
init_repo.py --sync-managed [--dry-run] lists the ones that apply to the repo and are newer than its
upgrades.reviewed version (homelab.yaml), as 'suggested, needs your yes'. Maintainers: add a note for
every release that adds something an existing repo has to adopt by hand.
Fields: version, id, kind (config | template | regenerate | manual), text, action, when, after_replace.
A template note whose file (file_lacks/file_has) has no local edits is settled by --sync-managed replacing the
file with the template (template-history.json); after_replace is what is left to do then (optional).
when (all must hold): component (enabled), config_empty (dotted key unset/empty), config_set (dotted key set),
file_lacks [path, text] (file exists and lacks text), file_has [path, text] (file exists and has text),
file_missing path (a file a release added is not in the repo; {template} is its template),
vmids_outside_ranges (snapshot VMIDs don't fit), agent_ips_unread (discovery/proxmox.json says the guest
agent IPs were not read: guest_ip_sources.agent present and not ok), default_site_implicit (two or more sites
and the default one has no ranges, VLANs without a site or no site_<default> group), multi_site (two or more
Placeholders in action and after_replace: {HM} skill dir, {template} template file of file_lacks, {detail} computed hint,

notes.text: check_env.py now verifies the Proxmox certificate and spots a private CA trusted only in the macOS keychain.
notes.action: Run `python3 {HM}/scripts/check_env.py` once; if it prints a proxmox.ca_cert hint, apply it with the user's yes.

notes.text: Optional vmid_scheme in homelab.yaml derives VM/LXC IDs from the network; your existing VMIDs don't follow vmid_ranges, so new IDs from the ranges would break your convention.
notes.action: {detail}

notes.text: The inventory could not read VM IPs from the guest agent; docs/proxmox-tokens.md has an optional section granting the read-only token the guest-agent privilege.
notes.action: If the user wants VM IPs: copy the 'Optional — VM IPs from the QEMU guest agent' paragraph and its pveum block from {template} into docs/proxmox-tokens.md, and have the user run those pveum lines on Proxmox (on /, next to PVEAuditor — never on /vms).

notes.text: proxmox_inventory.py --details now records the IPs running guests report; discovery/proxmox.json was made by an older version.
notes.action: Refresh it: `python3 {HM}/scripts/proxmox_inventory.py --details` (read-only).

notes.text: drift_report.py has a new 'Proxmox guests ↔ network' section matching scanned addresses to guests; it supersedes any hand-made guest/network mapping.
notes.action: After refreshing discovery/proxmox.json (--details) and network.json, re-run `python3 {HM}/scripts/drift_report.py`.

notes.text: The guest-agent section of docs/proxmox-tokens.md from 0.11.0 granted HomelabAgentAudit on /vms. That ACL replaces the PVEAuditor role inherited from /, so the read-only token loses VM.Audit and the inventory sees no guests. On Proxmox VE 9 PVEAuditor already covers the guest agent.
notes.action: Replace that section with the one in {template}. If the user ran the old /vms lines, have them undo them on Proxmox: `pveum acl delete /vms --users homelab@pve --roles HomelabAgentAudit` and `pveum acl delete /vms --tokens 'homelab@pve!ro' --roles HomelabAgentAudit` (then `pveum role delete HomelabAgentAudit` unless needed on 8.x), and refresh `python3 {HM}/scripts/proxmox_inventory.py --details`.

notes.text: check-updates.yml now merges into discovery/updates.json (each host with its own collected_at); the old play rewrote it with only the hosts of -e target=<group>.
notes.action: Replace the final 'Write discovery/updates.json' play of ansible/playbooks/check-updates.yml with the one in {template}, keeping any local edits above it.

notes.text: New patch-proxmox-node.yml patches one Proxmox node at a time: guests on shared storage are live-migrated (and back), HA guests go through node maintenance, pinned guests are shut down and restored. pve_node_plan.py makes its plan.
notes.action: If the user manages Proxmox nodes with Ansible: copy {template} and the tasks/pve-migrate.yml next to it into ansible/playbooks/ (new files).

file_lacks: Refuse hosts that need their own procedure

notes.text: patch-linux.yml can refuse hosts that need their own procedure (patch_requires_approval, set for Proxmox nodes in group_vars/proxmox_nodes.yml), so a broad -e target never patches and reboots a hypervisor.
notes.action: Copy the 'Refuse hosts that need their own procedure' pre-task from {template} into ansible/playbooks/patch-linux.yml, and add ansible/inventory/managed/group_vars/proxmox_nodes.yml from the same template directory if it is missing.

notes.text: New git.auto_push in homelab.yaml: push each verified commit to the remote (never force), so the repo is backed up off this Mac. check_env.py now reports commits not pushed to or not pulled from the upstream.
notes.action: If the repo has a remote (`git remote -v`), ask the user whether to push after each verified commit, then `python3 {HM}/scripts/config_set.py 'git.auto_push=true'` (or `=false`).

notes.text: New site.language in homelab.yaml: the language Claude replies in and writes docs, commit messages and new code comments in. Identifiers, plugin-managed files and skill issues stay English.
notes.action: Ask the user which language to use for this repo (default: the one they write in), then `python3 {HM}/scripts/config_set.py 'site.language=<code>'` (e.g. en, sk, de).

notes.text: The repo's CLAUDE.md has a new house rule about site.language.
notes.action: Copy the 'Language:' bullet from {template} into CLAUDE.md, under the house rules.

notes.text: Optional network.vlans in homelab.yaml names VLANs (id, name, cidr): --vlan accepts names, and the drift report labels addresses with them (#34).

notes.text: patch-linux.yml takes its batch size for independent hosts from ansible.patch_serial in homelab.yaml (#45); without it hosts are still patched one at a time. Cluster members and patch_requires_approval hosts always go one at a time.
notes.action: Ask the user how many independent hosts to patch at once (new repos use 5), then `python3 {HM}/scripts/config_set.py 'ansible.patch_serial=5'` with their value.

notes.text: Until 0.24.0, --sync-managed recorded upgrades.reviewed as soon as it listed suggestions, so ones that were postponed were never offered again (#67).
notes.action: Run `python3 {HM}/scripts/upgrade_notes.py --all` and go through the list with the user (this note is in it too): apply a suggestion they want, record each one they don't (or already turned down earlier) with `python3 {HM}/scripts/upgrade_notes.py --decline ID`, then `python3 {HM}/scripts/upgrade_notes.py --done recheck-hidden-suggestions` and run --sync-managed again.

notes.text: With two or more sites, a VLAN without a site applies to every site and an inventory host in no site group counts as the default site; the default site also needs ranges for reports to label its addresses (#65). check_env.py now warns about these (#63).
notes.action: Run `python3 {HM}/scripts/init_repo.py --name-default-site {site} --dry-run`, show the user each step (ranges, VLAN tags, site_{site} group) and run the ones they accept with `--steps`; a VLAN every site has gets `site: all` instead.

notes.text: Network scans know their site (#72): nmap_scan.py / ssh_probe.py --site <name> write discovery/network-<name>.json for a site other than the default, and network.excluded_hosts / discovery.ignore_unmanaged take {ip, site} entries (#66). discovery/network.json may still hold other sites' devices from earlier scans.
notes.action: Ask the user which sites were scanned into discovery/network.json. Rescan each other site from there with `nmap_scan.py <its ranges> --site <name>`, then remove its addresses from network.json if the ranges don't overlap the default site's (with overlapping ranges, start network.json over with a scan at the default site). Turn excluded or ignored addresses that hold at one site only into {ip, site} entries; check_env.py lists the ones inside shared ranges.
